title: Quadratic bandits with memory and an adversary adapted to delayed history.
summary: The current scalar quadratic loss acts on a window of recent actions, and the learner observes only one value generated by that window. The comparator uses the same fixed action throughout each window. Losses may depend on the actual history before the window; this history is held fixed in the comparison.

model.instance: Each action is $x_t\in[0,1]$, with fixed initial history $x_{1-m:0}=0$. Memory length $m\ge2$ includes the current action; two previous actions plus the current one correspond to $m=3$. $$f_t:[0,1]^m\to\mathbb R\ \text{is convex quadratic},\qquad |f_t(z)|\le B,\qquad\|\nabla f_t(z)\|_2\le L\quad(\forall z\in[0,1]^m).$$ The coefficients of $f_t$ may depend on history through $t-m$, but not more recent actions.

components.description: $T$ sequential rounds, or $T$ rounds per task

The learner's actions before round $1$ are zero. The displayed constant-$u$ comparator also uses $u$ before round $1$. Forcing the comparator to share the zero prehistory changes only the first $m-1$ terms, and the benchmarks differ by at most $2B(m-1)$; retain this finite-horizon difference. There is one scalar observation per round, $N=T$. All initialization and exploration are charged, with distinct information, arithmetic, communication, and memory resources.
